heading: Roles decide the folder, modifiers do not
body:
A MoneyService with Service belongs in services/MoneyService.<ext>. RequestRoute (a controller), Service, Store, HTTPClient (a client), Helper, Converter, Setup and Entity each require their standard suffix. They also require a lowercase plural folder that directly contains the file: controllers, services, stores, clients, helpers, converters, setups and entities. An IdentityProvider class also lives in controllers and ends with IdentityProvider. A role type for Allow is an empty class in server/roles, named after the role, such as server/roles/Admin.ts. The type name needs a domain prefix (a word for its subject, such as Money). The filename stem (the name without the extension) must match the type name with exact case. An annotated source file contains exactly one class and its imports. A worker and the project-root middleware follow the same rule, even without a framework marker. For a Rust impl, the compiler checks its target type. For a Go method, it checks the receiver type. Conflicting primary roles fail, so split the types into separate files. No second top-level class, function, interface, type alias, enum, constant, variable or statement is allowed. Pure data types belong in models/. Plain helper code becomes a static method of a utility class in client/utils or server/utils (a class whose name ends with Utils, with no annotation), or a method on the class that owns it. Annotated helper types need their own file. When the helper is a managed provider, use a role file such as helpers/PriceHelper.ts with Helper. Some helpers only add behavior, such as helpers/OrderInput.ts with Checked or helpers/Endpoint.ts with Setting. They live in their own files without Helper. So Tachyon does not treat their validation and configuration fields as injected dependencies. The compiler adds their behavior metadata. But it does not register them for dependency injection. In dependency injection, Tachyon creates the objects a class needs and gives them to it. Tachyon does not discover files with no framework annotations as providers. A Rust struct and all impl blocks for that same type form one class. A Go type and the methods on it also form one class. In other languages, nested types stay inside their owner. Violations fail with TY1310 before the compiler composes (joins) the generated units. The compiler joins separately checked files that you write into a generated program. That generated program may contain several behavior types. Modifiers such as Needs, Named, Table, WhenProfile, Settings, Checked and Setting do not add suffix or folder requirements. Both realms share every role except the controller (RequestRoute) and Stream (ADR 0031). A Tac service is client/services/<Name>Service, and a view addresses it as {name.field}. A Yon service is server/services/<Name>Service, and Tachyon injects it into a controller. A Yon controller is server/controllers/<Name>Controller, and its annotations declare its URLs. These are strict Tachyon conventions. Spring Boot does not require them.

`server/gateways/` is reserved. Tachyon writes the generated units of `@Gateway` class targets there, inside its own snapshot. A file that you write in that folder fails with `TY1310`.

This rule does not add a module linker (a tool that connects separate modules). Included role files still refuse relocatable relative dependency imports. Use the standard-library, virtual and realm-root import forms that the language supports. A worker Handler can keep its supported ordinary imports.
